segments.text: Two pins and two spring clips, pressed into every board by hand, one at a time. The clips tangle in bulk, and every part must sit flush.
segments.chapter: Press-fit pins and clips by hand

segments.text: This is the Southern Machinery S7040P pin insertion machine, set up for this board: four heads, four vibration bowl feeders, four press-fit parts.
A medium pin, a large pin, a medium multi-finger clip and a large one. Each has its own hole size, and each gets its own bowl and its own head.
The rule is simple. Bowl one feeds only head one, bowl two only head two, and so on. Each head presses one part, so there is no tooling change.
Every bowl delivers its part tail-down, and the two clip bowls are built to separate tangled spring fingers.
Here is the cycle. The board comes in on the conveyor, and the camera reads the fiducial marks, correcting each position to 0.015 millimetre.
Head one presses the medium pin, head two the large pin, head three the medium clip, and head four the large clip.
Pins are held below the open ring head and pressed on the rim only, so the clip inside the head is never touched.
A servo head presses each part until the pin shoulder or clip collar is flush, while a pedestal supports the board underneath.
The X-Y table moves to the next hole with 0.025 millimetre point-to-point accuracy. Each part takes about half a second.
If a part is missing, the machine stops and raises an alarm. Force detection with a log for every part is available as an option.
All four parts, one program. The finished board leaves the machine.
Boards from 50 by 50 up to 480 by 390 millimetres, 0.79 to 2.36 millimetres thick. Hole lists load from Excel by USB.
S7040P. Four bowls, four heads, four parts. Send us 200 of each part and five bare boards for a free sample run. Email info at smthelp dot com.

Insert pins, eyelets and terminals at 12,000 per hour.
Feed, orient, place and press four press-fit parts in one cell.

The S7020 is a dual-head insertion machine for bulk or reeled pins, eyelets and terminals. Vibration bowl or reel feeding, vision-corrected 0–360° insertion and inward/outward clinching replace the slowest manual job on your THT line.

Two pins and two multi-finger clips, all in bulk, pressed into plated through-holes. The S7040P gives each part its own vibration bowl and insertion head, aligns every board on its fiducials and presses each part flush with a servo head while a pedestal supports the board.
12,000 CPH with 2 insertion heads. Head count, feeders and tooling are configured to your parts.
Nozzles, grippers, press tools and bowl tracks are built per part and proven on your samples first.
How the S7020 removes manual pin work

What parts can the S7020 insert?

Pins, eyelets and terminals with a thickness of 0.5–1.2 mm, from bulk (vibration bowl) or reel. Other press-in parts can be reviewed with your drawings and samples.

Which steps does the S7040P cover?

All four: feeding from bulk bowls, tail-down orientation, fiducial-aligned placement and servo press-fit to flush. Hand soldering after insertion stays outside the cell.

S7020 or S7020T?

The S7020 is the flexible pin/eyelet/terminal machine for bulk or reel parts. The S7020T is optimised for reeled terminals and inline SMEMA production.

How do you handle tangled clips?

Each clip has its own vibration bowl, built to separate the spring fingers before the part reaches the track. This is proven on your samples first.

Is there a part change between sizes?

No. Each of the four parts has its own bowl, nozzle or gripper and press tool, so all four run in one program without changeover.

What do you need from us?

200+ of each part and 5 bare boards for a free sample run, plus the large-pin drawing, part count per position, and your press-force and flush-depth limits.

section.intro: One board cycle of the S7040P, step by step: the board is aligned on its fiducials, then each of the four heads presses its own part, fed from its own vibration bowl, until it sits flush.
section.canvas_label: Animated schematic of the S7040P: conveyor, fiducial camera, four vibration bowl feeders, four press heads, PCB pedestals, miss check and X-Y table
steps: The board with plated through-holes enters on the SMEMA conveyor and stops on the X-Y table.
The camera reads the board fiducials and corrects every hole position to 0.015 mm.
Bowl 1 feeds only Head 1. The pin is pressed on the rim of its head, never on the clip inside.
Bowl 2 feeds only Head 2, which presses only the large pin.
Bowl 3 separates tangled clips and feeds them tail-down to Head 3.
Bowl 4 feeds Head 4; the clip is pressed on its collar.
Each part is pressed until flush while a pedestal supports the board; a missing part stops the machine.
All four parts in one program with no tooling change; the board leaves the cell.

seo.description:
Two pins and two multi-finger clips, still pressed into every board by hand? The Southern Machinery S7040P PIN Insertion Machine feeds, orients, places and presses all four press-fit parts in one cell.

How it works
• One vibration bowl per bulk part, tail-down track; clip bowls built to separate tangled spring fingers.
• Fiducial vision: MARK correction 0.015 mm.
• Pins pressed on the rim only, clips on the collar, until flush; pedestal support under the board.
• X-Y positioning: point-to-point 0.025 mm, repeatability 0.05 mm. About 0.5 s per part.
• Miss check stops the machine; force detection with per-part log as an option.
• PCB 50 × 50 to 480 × 390 mm, 0.79–2.36 mm thick. Hole lists from Excel via USB.

Free sample run: send 200+ of each part and 5 bare boards.
